findings.title: Reconstructed recovery-codes credential loses its ID, breaking removeStoredCredentialById downstream
findings.body: In getCredentials() the stored CredentialModel myUser.recoveryCodes (created in updateCredential with setId(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId())) is discarded and replaced with a brand-new RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel built via RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...). createFromValues only accepts the raw codes, createdDate and userLabel, so the ID of the credential actually sitting in MyUser.recoveryCodes is not propagated to the returned model. RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator then does authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId()) using that ID. Because the ID no longer matches what was stored, and BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage does not implement removeStoredCredentialById/getStoredCredentialById anyway, the credential cannot be removed once all of the codes are consumed, leaving a stale 'all codes used' credential in federated storage.

findings.title: All-used recovery code credential is never removed when it lives in user storage
findings.body: After a successful recovery code match, the authenticator looks up the credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) which prefers getFederatedCredentialsStream(). If the credential is federated and allCodesUsed() is true, the code calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId()). CredentialManager.removeStoredCredentialById only operates on locally-stored credentials; the federated provider BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage does not implement removeStoredCredentialById at all. The credential therefore remains in the user storage with all codes consumed, and any subsequent regeneration depends on updateCredential overwriting it. Combined with the ID-mismatch in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials, the cleanup path is doubly broken for the very flow this PR introduces.

findings.title: Recovery codes are persisted in plaintext (raw unhashed) in credentialData
findings.body: updateCredential for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE stores input.getChallengeResponse() verbatim as credentialData, where getChallengeResponse() is the JSON array of raw generated codes that CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes. The standard keycloak-recovery-authn-codes provider hashes the codes before storing them in credentialData, so user-federated recovery codes now bypass that hashing. Anyone with read access to the credential metadata (admin REST /account/credentials, exports, debug logs, etc.) sees the usable plaintext recovery codes. Either hash them in the user-storage provider before storing or delegate to the standard provider for serialization while still returning a stored/federated credential model.

findings.title: Bean crashes with NoSuchElementException when user has no recovery-codes credential
findings.body: The constructor calls RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user).get() unconditionally. Before this PR the same .get() was already present, but the PR changes RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential to also fall back to federated credentials via getFederatedCredentialsStream. For federated users that have never configured recovery codes, getFederatedCredentialsStream still returns the provider's getCredentials() result; when MyUser.recoveryCodes is null the stream is empty and getCredential returns Optional.empty(), causing credentialModelOpt.get() to throw NoSuchElementException and break the login page. Guard with isPresent() and fall back to a sane default (or render no code-number UI) when no credential exists.

findings.title: hasRecoveryCodes does not normalize username but the map keys are lowercased
findings.body: addUser stores entries with users.put(translateUserName(username), new MyUser(username)) and translateUserName lowercases the username. hasRecoveryCodes looks up userPasswords.get(username) directly, so a caller passing a mixed-case username will always get false even when the user and their recovery codes exist. hasUserOTP has the same flaw; the new code copies it instead of fixing it. Pass the username through translateUserName (or use a case-insensitive lookup) so the assertion in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.assertUserHasRecoveryKeysCredentialInUserStorage works regardless of how the username is supplied.

findings.title: NPE / NumberFormatException on missing or malformed form params in processAction
findings.body: processAction reads generatedAtTimeString and generatedCodesString via formParamsMap.getFirst(...) and immediately compares them with .equals(...). If either parameter is missing, .getFirst returns null and the .equals call throws NullPointerException. The subsequent line uses Long.valueOf(generatedAtTimeString), which throws NumberFormatException if the value is present but not a valid long. This code is touched by the PR and is now invoked from the user-storage path too, so a tampered/missing form will throw before any attempt to clean up the generated auth-notes. Validate parameters first (treat null/blank as 'tampered' and re-issue via requiredActionChallenge).

findings.title: Test only exercises the happy path for recovery codes in user storage
findings.body: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only verifies create-in-user-storage + single successful login. It does not cover: regenerating codes (multiple updateCredential calls - which currently overwrites and changes the credential ID); using all codes until allCodesUsed() and observing what happens to the stored credential; disabling recovery codes through admin REST or account mgmt; account mgmt listing of credentials (which will show credentialData containing plaintext codes due to the hashing gap); and confirming that the credential is removed once all codes are used (which the production code path does not handle for federated storage). At minimum add a test that consumes every recovery code and asserts that the credential is actually gone, otherwise regressions in the cleanup path will not be caught.
